items.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003
items.q: The transcript mentions 'Pops' as a nickname used by Benny Goodman for the interviewee ('So Benny looked up like this. And he said, “stay up there, Pops.”'). There is no mention of Louis Armstrong in the text.

ctx.x: You had to pay your own.

Yeah. And you know you wonder, 90 bucks, how did I ever do that? So okay now a long thing goes on, and I know that Benny Goodman is rehearsing a new band. And I had also heard that he was getting a drummer every day. He didn’t like anybody or blah-blah-blah, whatever it was. So guys were telling me — there used to be a hangout in New York called Charlie’s Tavern, where everybody used to go because beers were a nickel and we could hang around there, drink beer, lie, you know tell a lot of lies. So anyway, this guy…

there and the band is playing and they were rehearsing this one tune three or four times through, five or six times through, whatever. And I’m listening to it. And I’m getting that down pretty good already, and I’ll see if I can play that tune. But you never know, you might have to go up there and sight read. So anyway I could read passably. I was not to what I developed into. But anyway they take a break. And so Benny said, “Eddie, how are you?” And he comes over and shakes his hand. And he says, “this is the…
